long_biography.plain_text:
Dick Pels’s books turned the sociology of intellectuals into a public argument about authority, representation and political style. His scholarship examined intellectual rivalry and the changing tempo of academic life, while later volumes addressed populism, national identity and European solidarity. He continued contributing essays and commentary to Dutch political debate long after leaving university teaching.

Pels eventually returned to a creative practice that predated his academic work. He had played bass and lead guitar in rock bands during the 1960s and 1970s, then resumed writing and performing original songs after retirement. Across three folk-rock albums, he combined melody with the reflective writing that also marks his political and sociological work.
